Split variables into within-person and between-person parts

Source: R/stats_preprocess.R
split_levels.Rd

Person-mean centring (Curran & Bauer, 2011). Adds two columns for every variable: <var>_between, the person's mean, which is the stable level that distinguishes one person from another (repeated on each of the person's rows), and <var>_within, the deviation of each occasion from that stable level. The original columns are kept. A regression on both columns estimates separate within-person and between-person slopes. split_wb() is a short alias.

Usage

split_levels(data, id, vars, time = NULL, keep_all = TRUE)

split_wb(data, id, vars, time = NULL, keep_all = TRUE)

Arguments

data

Long-format data frame.

id

Person identifier column.

vars

Columns to split (any fit_lm() selector).

time

Optional time column, kept in the output with keep_all = FALSE.

keep_all

Keep every column of data (default). With FALSE, only the id and time columns, the split variables, and their _between and _within parts are returned.

Value

data with <var>_within and <var>_between columns appended.

References

Curran, P. J., & Bauer, D. J. (2011). The disaggregation of within-person and between-person effects in longitudinal models of change. Annual Review of Psychology, 62, 583-619. doi:10.1146/annurev.psych.093008.100356

Examples

split_levels(srl, id = "name", vars = "efficacy") |> head()
#>    name day efficacy    value planning monitoring   effort  control help social

#> 4 Aisha   4 55.88235 63.88889 65.90909  22.368421 93.65079 42.42424   24   47.5
#> 5 Aisha   5 55.88235 36.11111 52.27273  22.368421 71.42857 57.57576   48   57.5
